defects.name: Short Shot
defects.description: Part is incomplete — the melt froze or ran out before the cavity filled. Shows at the far end of flow, thin walls, or behind trapped air.
quickCheck: Is Min Cushion still there, or did it hit zero?
Is Fill Peak flatlined at the Maximum Filling Pressure limit?
All cavities short, or just some?

causes.cause: Not enough material committed before transfer
causes.fix: Move V-P transfer later (lower the position number) or increase dose position (shot size)

causes.cause: Pressure-limited fill — machine can't hold set speed
causes.fix: Raise Maximum Filling Pressure to restore headroom (10-20% above Fill Peak)

causes.cause: Melt or mold too cold — front freezing off
causes.fix: Raise barrel temps and/or mold temp; raise fill velocity so the front runs hotter

causes.cause: Trapped gas blocking the last-to-fill area
causes.fix: Clean vents; try lower clamp force; slow the final fill stage so gas can escape

causes.cause: Check ring leaking — melt slipping backward
causes.fix: Run Flow-Check / watch cushion repeatability; schedule check-ring service

causes.cause: Nozzle or gate partially blocked (cold slug)
causes.fix: Raise nozzle temp slightly; verify suck back isn't freezing the tip

diagnosticSteps: Confirm cushion exists — zero cushion means shot size / transfer, stop there
Check Fill Peak vs the pressure limit — if clipped, fix the limit before anything else
One cavity short in a multi-cavity tool = tool issue (vent/gate), not process
Only then adjust temperature or speed, one change at a time

defects.name: Flash
defects.description: Thin skin of plastic squeezed out at the parting line, vents, or around pins — the mold was forced open or the melt found a gap.
quickCheck: Did All Peak jump above Fill Peak? (transfer spike)
Is actual clamp force at setpoint?
New flash on an old mold, or old mold just worn?

causes.cause: Transfer too late — cavity overfilled on velocity
causes.fix: Raise the V-P transfer position (transfer earlier)

causes.cause: Pack too aggressive
causes.fix: Lower 1st hold pressure, or lower H.V. Limit to soften the transfer spike

causes.cause: Clamp tonnage low vs cavity pressure
causes.fix: Verify actual clamp = setpoint (correction ON); raise clamp force only after that checks out

causes.cause: Melt too thin (hot)
causes.fix: Lower barrel temps and/or fill velocity — watch Fill Peak fall as viscosity rises

causes.cause: Mold worn or debris on the parting line
causes.fix: Inspect and clean faces; flash localized in one spot is usually steel, not process

diagnosticSteps: Where is it? All around = tonnage/overpack; one spot = tool or debris
Check All Peak vs Fill Peak — a spike at transfer is the classic new-flash cause
Confirm tonnage isn't decaying (Clamp F at Hold End)
Then walk hold pressure down in small steps

defects.name: Burn Marks (Dieseling)
defects.description: Black or brown scorched spots, usually at end-of-fill or dead corners — trapped air compressed so fast it ignited and charred the melt.
quickCheck: Did clamp force get raised lately?

causes.cause: Vents blocked or crushed shut
causes.fix: Clean vents; try LOWER clamp force — over-tonnage crushes vents closed

causes.cause: Fill too fast at end of flow — air can't escape
causes.fix: Lower the last fill-stage velocity, or add a slow final stage

causes.cause: Pressure spike at transfer slamming trapped gas
causes.fix: Raise V-P position (transfer earlier)

causes.cause: Melt too hot — chars easily
causes.fix: Lower barrel temps, back pressure, screw RPM

diagnosticSteps: Fixed location = venting; clean vents and retest before touching process
Slow only the final 10-15% of fill — don't give up your whole fill speed
If it started after a tonnage increase, that's your answer

defects.name: Weld / Knit Lines
defects.description: A visible line (and weak spot) where two flow fronts met — downstream of holes, cores, or multiple gates. Cold fronts don't knit.
quickCheck: Cosmetic problem, strength problem, or both?
Is there a vent at the meeting point?
Mold temp actually at setpoint on the steel?

causes.cause: Flow fronts too cold when they meet
causes.fix: Raise fill velocity; raise melt and mold temps — hotter fronts knit stronger and fainter

causes.cause: Not packed together after meeting
causes.fix: Raise hold pressure so the joint gets forged, verify gate seal covers it

causes.cause: Gas trapped exactly at the knit point
causes.fix: Vent at the weld location; lower clamp if vents are being crushed

causes.cause: Gate location puts the weld in a bad spot
causes.fix: Tool change — move/resize gate or add flow leader (design fix, log it)

diagnosticSteps: Raise mold temp first — biggest weld-line lever for cosmetics
Then fill speed, watching for burn at the same spot (venting)
Strength-critical welds may need the tooling fix, not process

defects.name: Sink Marks
defects.description: Shallow depressions on the surface opposite thick sections, ribs, or bosses — the core stayed molten, kept shrinking, and pulled the skin in.
quickCheck: Was hold time proven past gate seal?

causes.cause: Not enough pack
causes.fix: Raise 1st hold pressure in steps; confirm Pack P. actually reaches setpoint

causes.cause: Gate not sealed when hold ends — pack leaks back out
causes.fix: Raise hold time; run a gate-seal (weight) study

causes.cause: Cushion collapsing — nothing left to pack with
causes.fix: Raise dose position to restore cushion; investigate check ring if it wanders

causes.cause: Melt too hot — more volumetric shrink than pack can replace
causes.fix: Lower barrel temps modestly

causes.cause: Mold too hot over the sink area
causes.fix: Lower mold temp / check the cooling circuit behind that face

diagnosticSteps: Weigh parts while stepping hold time up — weight plateau = gate seal; sinks past that point aren't a time problem
Then step hold pressure up, watching flash and dimensions
Persistent sink over a thick boss with everything maxed = design/thickness, log it

defects.name: Voids / Bubbles
defects.description: Hollow pockets inside the part (cut one open to confirm). Vacuum voids come from shrinkage in thick sections; gas voids come from air or volatiles carried in the melt.
quickCheck: Void round and in the thickest section? (vacuum)
Bubbles visible in a purge patty?

causes.cause: Vacuum void — thick core shrank unpacked
causes.fix: Raise hold pressure and hold time; raise mold temp so the skin stays packable longer

causes.cause: Moisture gassing in the melt
causes.fix: Verify drying (dewpoint, time, temp) before touching the press

causes.cause: Air pulled in by decompression
causes.fix: Lower after-dose pull back distance

causes.cause: Air trapped during recovery
causes.fix: Raise back pressure to squeeze air out of the melt

diagnosticSteps: Cut the part: smooth round void in thick center = vacuum → pack harder; scattered irregular bubbles = gas → dryness/decompression
Purge and look for foam or bubbles in the patty
Fix gas at the source; don't try to pack gas away

defects.name: Splay / Silver Streaks
defects.description: Silver or off-color streaks fanning across the surface in the flow direction, usually from the gate — gas (steam, air, or degradation volatiles) smeared along the skin.
quickCheck: Dryer: dewpoint, temp, and actual hours in the hopper?

causes.cause: Moisture in the resin (the big one)
causes.fix: Fix drying — dewpoint around -40, correct temp, full residence; check for condensation and dryer bypass

causes.cause: Melt overheating / degrading
causes.fix: Lower barrel temps, screw RPM, and back pressure; check residence time isn't excessive

causes.cause: Air sucked into the nozzle by decompression
causes.fix: Lower after-dose pull back until gate-area splay stops

causes.cause: Shear splay at the gate
causes.fix: Lower the first fill-stage velocity through the gate

causes.cause: Drool / cold material smeared in
causes.fix: Trim nozzle temp; balance with suck back

diagnosticSteps: Always rule out moisture first — pull a sample and verify drying, don't trust the schedule
Streaks only at the gate = decompression air or gate shear; everywhere = moisture or melt temp
Change one variable, run 10 shots, judge
defects.notes: Hygroscopic resins (PC, PA/nylon, PBT, ABS) will splay from moisture you can't see or feel. PC and nylon also lose strength (hydrolysis) — wet molding hurts more than cosmetics.

defects.name: Flow Lines / Record Grooves
defects.description: Ripples, halos, or ring patterns on the surface tracking the flow front — the front moved too slowly or unevenly and each hesitation printed.
quickCheck: Do rings match a velocity stage change position?

causes.cause: Flow front too cold/slow — printing as it creeps
causes.fix: Raise fill velocity; raise mold temp

causes.cause: Melt too cold
causes.fix: Raise barrel temps

causes.cause: Visible hesitation at a stage break
causes.fix: Smooth the profile — move or remove the stage transition

causes.cause: Under-packed surface not replicating steel
causes.fix: Raise hold pressure

diagnosticSteps: Raise mold temp and fill speed first — the classic pair for this defect
If a ring sits exactly where a velocity change happens, that's your smoking gun
Confirm no burn appears at end-of-fill as you speed up

defects.name: Gloss Variation
defects.description: Patchy shiny/dull areas — surface replication of the steel varied, from uneven mold temperature, uneven packing, or flow behavior.
quickCheck: Dull patch over one cooling circuit?

causes.cause: Mold surface temperature uneven
causes.fix: Check every cooling circuit flow; balance halves; pyrometer-map the steel

causes.cause: Packing uneven — dull where pressure is low
causes.fix: Raise hold pressure / hold time; verify gate seal

causes.cause: Fill speed changes printing gloss bands
causes.fix: Smooth the velocity profile

causes.cause: Tool surface condition (polish/texture wear, deposits)
causes.fix: Clean/inspect the cavity surface — outgassing deposits dull steel over a run

diagnosticSteps: Map the dull zones against cooling circuits first
Higher mold temp generally = higher, more even gloss
If gloss shifts over a run with no setting change: deposits on the steel

defects.name: Jetting
defects.description: A worm-like squiggle on the surface starting at the gate — melt shot across the cavity as a rope instead of flowing as a front, then froze.
quickCheck: First-stage speed high through the gate?

causes.cause: Melt jets through the gate too fast
causes.fix: Lower the 1st fill-stage velocity until flow lays down, then speed up after the gate

causes.cause: Cold slug fired into the cavity
causes.fix: Raise nozzle temp slightly; check suck back isn't freezing the tip; verify cold-slug well

causes.cause: Melt too cold and stiff — ropes instead of fans
causes.fix: Raise barrel temps

causes.cause: Gate geometry aims flow into open space
causes.fix: Tooling: impinge flow against a wall/pin, or enlarge gate (log it)

diagnosticSteps: Slow ONLY the gate stage — add a stage break just past the gate and restore speed after
If a cold blemish rides the jet, chase nozzle temp / cold slug
Still jetting slow and hot = gate design

defects.name: Gate Blush
defects.description: A hazy, dull, or discolored halo right at the gate — high shear tearing the surface as melt rams through the smallest opening in the system.
quickCheck: Melt temp low (stiff melt shears worse)?

causes.cause: Too much shear through the gate
causes.fix: Lower 1st-stage fill velocity through the gate

causes.cause: Melt too cold at the gate
causes.fix: Raise barrel/nozzle temps a step

causes.cause: Pack slamming the gate area
causes.fix: Soften transfer (H.V. Limit) or taper hold with a lower 2nd stage

causes.cause: Gate too small or sharp-edged
causes.fix: Tooling: open/radius the gate (log it)

diagnosticSteps: Slow the gate stage first — blush responds fast if shear is the cause
Then a modest melt-temp bump
No response = gate steel

defects.name: Stringing
defects.description: Fine threads of plastic trailing from the nozzle or gates when the mold opens — melt at the tip stayed fluid and pulled into strings.
quickCheck: Hot runner tips or cold sprue?

causes.cause: Not enough decompression
causes.fix: Raise after-dose pull back in 0.5 mm steps until strings stop

causes.cause: Nozzle/tip too hot
causes.fix: Lower nozzle temp in small steps

causes.cause: Residual melt pressure at mold open
causes.fix: Enable/raise Ret Vel after hold, or add a small dose delay

causes.cause: Wrong nozzle tip style for the material
causes.fix: Hardware: consider a shut-off or reverse-taper tip for stubborn resins (log it)

diagnosticSteps: Suck back up in small steps — stop at the first clean shot (too much causes splay)
Then nozzle temp down a notch at a time
Nylon is the classic stringer — expect to balance both

defects.name: Drooling
defects.description: Melt oozing from the nozzle between shots — puddles on the sprue bushing, cold slugs next shot, and blemishes at the gate.
quickCheck: Fill Start Position drifting? (pressure pushing screw)
Moisture? Wet resin gasses and drools

causes.cause: Melt pressure left in front of the screw
causes.fix: Raise after-dose pull back; consider Ret Vel

causes.cause: Nozzle too hot
causes.fix: Lower nozzle temp

causes.cause: Moisture gassing pushes melt out
causes.fix: Verify drying

causes.cause: Long open time lets the tip drain
causes.fix: Reduce interval/handling time, or add dose delay so melt is prepared later

diagnosticSteps: Watch the tip for one full cycle — when does it drip?
Check Fill Start Position shot-to-shot; drift = pressure escaping out the nozzle
Balance suck back vs nozzle temp; recheck for splay after changes

defects.name: Warpage
defects.description: Part twists, bows, or cups after ejection — one region shrank more than another. Differential shrinkage is always the mechanism; the cause is what made it differential.
quickCheck: Core vs cavity water temps equal?
Warp direction consistent shot to shot?

causes.cause: Uneven mold cooling — one face hotter
causes.fix: Balance/verify every circuit (flow, not just temp); equalize halves

causes.cause: Ejected too hot — part finishes shrinking unrestrained
causes.fix: Raise cooling time; consider a cooling fixture

causes.cause: Overpack near the gate vs starved far end
causes.fix: Lower 1st hold, use a tapered 2nd stage; verify even fill

causes.cause: Fiber orientation (glass-filled)
causes.fix: Change fill speed to alter orientation; often a gate-location problem (log it)

causes.cause: High molded-in stress from cold mold/melt
causes.fix: Raise mold temp so the part relaxes in the tool

diagnosticSteps: Thermal-map both halves — a 10 degree imbalance is enough to warp
Add cooling time as a test: warp improves = ejection temp; doesn't = packing/orientation
Adjust pack profile last; measure after 24h (parts keep moving)

defects.name: Dimensional Drift / Inconsistency
defects.description: Dimensions wander shot-to-shot or across a run with nothing 'changed' — the process is leaking consistency somewhere. Part weight is your best tracer.
quickCheck: Anything thermal still soaking (machine, mold, dryer)?

causes.cause: Cushion wandering — check ring leaking
causes.fix: Run Flow-Check; verify dose repeatability; service the ring

causes.cause: Gate seal marginal — some shots seal, some don't
causes.fix: Raise hold time past the weight plateau with margin

causes.cause: Pressure-limited fill on some shots
causes.fix: Restore headroom above Fill Peak

causes.cause: Tonnage drifting with temperature
causes.fix: Confirm Auto Clamp Force Correction ON and tracking

causes.cause: Melt inconsistency — feed, drying, regrind ratio
causes.fix: Stabilize back pressure/RPM; check throat temp; audit material handling

diagnosticSteps: Weigh 30 consecutive parts — weight scatter maps the problem: with cushion scatter = check ring; with fill-time scatter = fill control
Fix consistency before chasing the nominal dimension
Only then move the mean with hold pressure (bigger) or less pack (smaller)

defects.name: Black Specks / Contamination
defects.description: Dark flecks scattered in the part — charred resin flaking off from dead spots, degraded material, or dirty regrind riding through.
quickCheck: Specks in the virgin material itself?
How long since a proper purge/screw pull?
Residence time long (small shot, big barrel)?

causes.cause: Degraded resin coating the screw/barrel breaking loose
causes.fix: Aggressive purge (commercial purge compound); if it returns fast, schedule a screw pull

causes.cause: Running too hot for too long
causes.fix: Lower barrel temps, back pressure, RPM; reduce residence (dose delay, cycle discipline)

causes.cause: Contaminated material path
causes.fix: Inspect hopper, loader, grinder, and regrind for foreign material and cross-contamination

causes.cause: Barrel/screw wear — plating or steel flakes
causes.fix: Maintenance inspection if specks are metallic or persistent after purging

diagnosticSteps: Purge to clean, then time how long until specks return — minutes = active degradation; days = deposits
Check specks with a magnifier: charred plastic vs metal vs foreign
Audit residence: shot size well under 20% of barrel capacity means material is cooking in there

defects.name: Brittleness
defects.description: Parts crack or snap under loads they should survive — the polymer chains got shortened (degraded) or the part is full of stress or bad welds.
quickCheck: Was the resin dry AT molding (PC/PA hydrolyze wet)?
Break always at a weld line?

causes.cause: Hydrolysis — molded wet (PC, nylon, PBT)
causes.fix: Fix drying; wet molding permanently destroys strength even when parts look fine

causes.cause: Thermal degradation
causes.fix: Lower barrel temps, RPM, back pressure; cut residence time

causes.cause: Too much / too many-pass regrind
causes.fix: Cap regrind ratio; audit what's actually going in the blender

causes.cause: Weak weld lines
causes.fix: See Weld Lines — hotter fronts, more pack

causes.cause: Molded-in stress
causes.fix: Raise mold temp; lower hold; avoid cold-fast-stressed processing

diagnosticSteps: Where does it break? Weld line = knit problem; random = material degradation
Verify drying records and melt temp vs datasheet
Mold a batch at datasheet-nominal everything with verified-dry virgin resin — if strength returns, work back to find the abuse

defects.name: Delamination
defects.description: Surface peels in flaky layers like an onion — layers of the part never bonded, usually from contamination or a cold, over-sheared skin.
quickCheck: Material contamination possible (wrong regrind, unpurged resin)?

causes.cause: Incompatible resin mixed in
causes.fix: Full purge; audit material handling and grinder for cross-contamination

causes.cause: Cold melt sheared into layers
causes.fix: Raise barrel temps; lower gate-stage velocity

causes.cause: Too much mold release / surface contamination
causes.fix: Stop the spray; clean the tool — release agent is a bond-breaker between layers

causes.cause: Moisture films between layers
causes.fix: Verify drying

diagnosticSteps: Peel a flake and burn-test/compare it — contamination is the most common answer
Eliminate mold release entirely as a test
Then melt temp up, gate shear down

defects.name: Color Streaks / Poor Mixing
defects.description: Swirls or streaks of uneven color — colorant never got homogenized into the melt, or a second material is riding along.
quickCheck: Streaks appear after a color change? (old color purging out)

causes.cause: Not enough mixing work in recovery
causes.fix: Raise back pressure; a modest RPM increase adds mixing too

causes.cause: Masterbatch dosing/carrier problem
causes.fix: Verify let-down ratio and that the carrier resin matches the base

causes.cause: Rear barrel too cold — pigment not dispersing
causes.fix: Raise rear zone temps a step

causes.cause: Incomplete color change purge
causes.fix: Purge properly (patties until clean); check dead spots in nozzle/tip

diagnosticSteps: Back pressure up first — the #1 mixing knob
Verify the blender/doser actually feeding at ratio
Persistent streaks with everything right = consider a mixing nozzle/screw (hardware)

defects.name: Unmelts
defects.description: Visible solid granules or gels in the part — pellets got to the front of the screw without fully melting.
quickCheck: Shot size huge for the barrel?

causes.cause: Not enough melting energy in recovery
causes.fix: Raise back pressure; lower screw RPM (slower transport = more melting time per flight)

causes.cause: Rear/mid zones too cold
causes.fix: Raise rear and middle barrel temps

causes.cause: Shot too big for the barrel — residence too short
causes.fix: If shot uses most of the stroke, the machine is undersized for the job (flag it)

causes.cause: High-melt-point contaminant in the blend
causes.fix: Audit material/regrind for a different polymer

diagnosticSteps: Purge patty check — unmelts visible in the purge confirms it's upstream of the mold
Slow RPM + raise BP together, retest
Then rear zones up in 5-10 degree steps

defects.name: Cracking / Stress Whitening
defects.description: Cracks or white stress marks, at ejection or days later — molded-in or mechanically applied stress exceeded what the material could carry.
quickCheck: Cracks at ejector pins / around cores? (mechanical)
Delayed cracking in the field? (residual stress + chemicals)

causes.cause: Overpacking — residual stress especially near the gate
causes.fix: Lower 1st hold pressure; taper with 2nd stage

causes.cause: Ejection stress — part too hot or gripped too hard
causes.fix: Raise cooling time; slow/soften ejector; slow mold-open breakaway

causes.cause: Cold mold = high molded-in stress
causes.fix: Raise mold temp

causes.cause: Degraded/brittle material
causes.fix: See Brittleness — drying, temps, regrind

causes.cause: Sharp corners / thin bosses concentrating stress
causes.fix: Design: add radii (log for tooling)

diagnosticSteps: Location tells the story: pin circles = ejection; gate area = pack; random+delayed = stress+environment
Cooling time up as a quick test for ejection-driven cracks
Then walk hold pressure down watching sinks on the other side

defects.name: Part / Sprue Sticking
defects.description: Part hangs in the cavity or on the core, or the sprue stays in the bushing — release forces beat the ejection system.

causes.cause: Overpacked — part gripping the steel
causes.fix: Lower hold pressure/time; transfer a touch earlier

causes.cause: Too hot at ejection — soft part grabbing
causes.fix: Raise cooling time; check mold temp

causes.cause: Sprue sticking: nozzle/bushing mismatch
causes.fix: Check nozzle radius and orifice (nozzle hole must be SMALLER than bushing hole); verify sprue puller; cool the sprue more

causes.cause: Ejection can't overcome release force
causes.fix: More stroke/pressure or a second count — but treat as a band-aid

causes.cause: Tool condition — polish, draft, undercuts, damage
causes.fix: Inspect for drag marks and burrs; polish in draft direction (tool room)

diagnosticSteps: Which half it sticks to points at that half's release problem
Lower pack first — overpack is the most common process cause
Only reach for stronger ejection after pack and cooling are ruled out

defects.name: Ejector Pin Marks
defects.description: Visible circles, gloss spots, sink-like depressions, or stress rings where the pins push — the part was too soft or the push too hard for the material to take.

causes.cause: Part too hot when pushed
causes.fix: Raise cooling time

causes.cause: Ejection too fast/hard
causes.fix: Lower ejector velocity and pressure

causes.cause: High release force making pins work too hard
causes.fix: Lower hold (overpack); see Sticking

causes.cause: Pins mis-set or too small for the push (tool)
causes.fix: Tool room: pin flush/protrusion check; larger or more pins if chronic

diagnosticSteps: Cooling time up 20% as a test — marks fade = temperature
Then soften ejection
Marks on a cold, gently-ejected part = pin fit/tool issue
